scope: Unpacked Manifest V3 development extension with an explicitly reviewed, local read task on the active Chrome tab. This mission does not include authenticated model planning, consequential actions, or a Web Store release.

keep: Canonical scheduler, hosted Browser Worker, model gateway and production services
extend: Chrome side panel and deterministic active-tab read executor for local development

schemaImpact.rollout: No database changes. Load the extension unpacked in a test browser profile.

auth.description: No Xroga session, token exchange or new login surface.

tenant.description: No cross-tenant data handling or server access. The selected Chrome profile owns its tab.

approval.description: Explicit review for a local page read, bound to a tab, URL and document. No authority to write or spend.

credentials.description: No extension credentials or access to password fields, cookies or browser storage.

egress.description: Page content can move only from the user-approved tab into ephemeral local extension UI. The extension has no outbound data path.

cost.description: No cloud browser, worker service, model call or paid tool.

tests.scope: Four passing checks for local plan grammar, unsupported actions, URL scope and minimum permissions.

Passed in Chrome 156.0.8078.81 on isolated HTTPS fixtures. Verified real side-panel opening, rendered report through the same extension page, private fields excluded, cancellation, same-URL reload rejection, cross-origin denial and zero model calls.

architecture.reason: A local browser execution primitive has no scheduler, model dispatch, backend routes or authority for consequential actions.

rollout: Review the development branch and install unpacked in a test profile. Public release requires separate package, privacy and Chrome Web Store gates.
rollback: Unload or remove the unpacked extension. There is no persisted task or server state to migrate.
knownGaps: Authenticated model planning and the existing canonical approval integration remain to be implemented.
Meta Ads draft or publishing workflow has not been tested.
No Chrome Web Store review, public listing or production verification.

blockers: Public release needs independent install/security review, privacy disclosures and Chrome Web Store submission.
